article_title: Domain-Specific Modeling Languages in Computer-Based Learning Environments: a Systematic Approach to Support Science Learning through Computational Modeling
citation: Nicole M. Hutchins & Gautam Biswas & Ningyu Zhang & Caitlin Snyder & Ákos Lédeczi & Miklós Maróti. (2020). Domain-Specific Modeling Languages in Computer-Based Learning Environments: a Systematic Approach to Support Science Learning through Computational Modeling. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-020-00209-z
title: C2STEM environment: DSML-based collaborative computational STEM learning environment built on Snap!
description: C2STEM is the authors' "Collaborative, Computational STEM (C2STEM) learning environment" in which the DSML structures "form a core component". It is "built on top of the Snap! block-structured programming language", embeds domain-specific blocks (e.g., set and change blocks for kinematics variables), and adds data collection support through "graphing and table tools that capture the updates in selected DSML variables at each simulation step". DSMLs were implemented in it for Kinematics, Marine Biology, and Earth Science units.
requirements: An underlying block-based programming environment (Snap!) providing general-purpose blocks such as conditionals and variables
constraints: The authors note that similarities among block-based environments (Alice, App Lab, App Inventor, Scratch, NetTango, Snap!) make the DSML approach generalizable to many environments, but the implementation described targets Snap!
target_learners: upper elementary through high school science students
target_learning_goals: kinematics, coral reef biology, and water runoff concepts
examples: Fig. 5 shows a C2STEM task in which students simulate the horizontal motion of a sloth given starting position, velocity, and constant acceleration values.
